text:
A: Hello! Hi, can you hear me okay?
B: Yes. Hi.
A: I'm Marites. Sorry, my phone is on the rice cooker, hehe.
B: Claire. That's fine.
A: How are you finding it? The calls?
B: All right. They go quickly.
A: Yeah, very quick. Three minutes is nothing. Erm, so what do you do, Claire?
B: I'm a midday supervisor at a primary school. Dinner lady, basically.
A: Oh, that's nice. My son is at primary. Rafael, he's nine.
B: Mine's nine. Alfie.
A: Oh! Same age. Year four or five?
B: Year four.
A: Rafael too. Do you have the World Book Day? I forgot until the night before, oh my God. I was cutting cardboard at eleven o'clock at night.
B: Yeah, it's mad. Half of them come as footballers now and say it's from a book. What did he go as?
A: Erm, a Minecraft man. With a box on his head. I don't know if Minecraft is a book, to be honest.
B: There are Minecraft books, so you're technically fine. Alfie's obsessed with it as well. He talks about nothing else. I don't understand a word.
A: Same! Every night, Mummy, look, I built a house. And I say very nice, but I don't know what I'm looking at, hehe.
B: That's about the level of it, yeah.
A: And what do you, erm, what do you do at the lunch? You watch the children?
B: Yeah, in the hall and out on the playground. Stop fights, stop them playing football through the windows. The food's got worse since the new contractor came in, so a lot of it ends up in the bin.
A: Oh no. That's a shame. What do they give?
B: Pale pasta. Beige things. You'd be horrified, honestly. You look like someone who actually cooks.
A: Hehe, yes, I cook every night. Filipino food. Adobo, sinigang, rice always. I make too much, always too much. Jun takes it to work.
B: What's sinigang?
A: It's like a soup, sour soup, with tamarind. Pork or fish, with vegetables. Very good when it's cold.
B: That sounds good, actually. I'd try that.
A: You should! Erm, what do you do, sorry, I mean, my job, I'm a carer. Home care. I visit old people in their houses.
B: That's a hard job.
A: Sometimes. But I like the people. One lady, every time, she gives me a biscuit and says, sit, sit, you look tired. I'm supposed to help her, and she's looking after me.
B: Ha. That's quite nice, actually. More than I get at work.
A: No biscuits?
B: Not from the other staff. I bring my own. Rich tea.
A: Hehe, I saw them in your picture, next to the books. You read a lot?
B: Yeah. Mostly secondhand, from the Oxfam. Are you a reader?
A: No, honestly, not really. I watch the Filipino dramas on YouTube. The same ones again and again. My husband says, you know what happens, why you watch. I say, I like to cry at the same part.
